name: Engalm
kurzbeschreibung: The historic Engalm village at the Great Sycamore Plain (Großer Ahornboden) in the Karwendel is Tyrol's oldest active mountain pasture village.
oeffnungszeiten: Mitte Mai bis Ende Oktober täglich 08:30–18:00 Uhr
beschreibung:
Overview

The heritage-listed Engalm in the upper Riß Valley is recognized as Tyrol's oldest documented mountain pasture village, boasting more than a millennium of pastoral tradition. Nestled at approximately 1,200 metres above sea level at the head of the valley, the settlement forms the crowning jewel of the famous Großer Ahornboden nature reserve within Karwendel Nature Park. Surrounded by over two thousand ancient sycamore maple trees—many of which have weathered over six centuries—beneath the sheer vertical limestone crags of the Karwendel mountains, the village appears frozen in time. More than fifteen historic log cabins, an artisan show dairy, and a charming wooden chapel stand as authentic monuments to alpine transhumance, where farmers still spend summers crafting award-winning raw-milk mountain cheese.

Route & Requirements

A visit to the Engalm is a relaxing and scenic experience for visitors of all ages, requiring no physical exertion. From the spacious car park at the end of the toll road, a wide, gravelled footpath leads directly into the alpine village in an easy ten-minute stroll. The trail is completely level and fully accessible for wheelchairs and strollers. Within the hamlet, an informative educational nature trail explains the ancient dairy techniques and centuries-old farming rhythms. For energetic hikers, the Eng serves as a premier trailhead for classic alpine tours toward the Binsalm, Falkenhütte, or the dramatic Lamsenspitze.

Visiting & Getting There

The Eng is accessed by road exclusively through Hinterriß along the panoramic, scenic Rißtal toll road. During summer, the Karwendel mountain hiker bus runs regularly from Lenggries and Tegernsee train stations directly to the Eng terminus. Spacious parking is available at the end of the valley. The village, farm cheese boutique, and alpine inn are open daily from early May through late October. The road is closed in winter due to snow.

Tips

Do not miss visiting the Engalm show dairy to sample authentic Enger mountain cheese, produced exclusively from fresh hay milk. The most magical time to visit is in autumn (late September to mid-October), when the ancient maples of the Großer Ahornboden blaze in magnificent shades of gold and amber. Relax on the sun terrace of the Almgasthof Eng with fresh Kaiserschmarrn pancakes before purchasing artisanal cheese to take home.
